newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Flamboyant Bogota mayor to run for presidency.
newsitem.headline: Flamboyant Bogota mayor to run for presidency.

text.p: Bogota's colourful mayor, Antanas Mockus, said on Wednesday he would resign within a month to contest next year's presidential elections.
Mockus said he had his eye on the top job but did not rule out running for the vice-presidency on a joint ticket with Chief Prosecutor Alfonso Valdivieso.
Mockus' headline-grabbing antics have included baring his backside in public and getting married in a tigers' cage.
A ticket combining him with Valdivieso, a fervent anti-drug crusader, would be a sure vote-winner, according to the most recent opinion polls.
"At the right moment I will present my resignation and go down that path (of the presidential race)," Mockus told the Radionet radio network.

"In principle I would be running for the presidency but I don't rule out accompanying somebody...it could be an alternative me as vice-president and him (Valdivieso) as presidential candidate," he added.

In an opinion poll published a week ago by Cromos magazine, Valdivieso emerged as favourite, with 23 percent of those surveyed saying they would vote for him if elections were held immediately. Mockus was joint third with 12 percent voter support.
Interior Minister Horacio Serpa, President Ernesto samper's right-hand man, was placed second with 18 percent of the 1,200 people surveyed saying they would vote for him.
Mockus, a self-described "neo-anarchist" and academic with a passion for mathematics and metaphysics, took office in January 1995 and would normally step down next December.
Under Colombian law, however, anybody seeking to run for the presidency must resign from public office a year before elections, which are scheduled for May 1998.
